scientific_goal: Determine which drift parameter block turns the finite-particle multistep GMM objective into improved long-rollout amplitude and energy, while preventing the MC term from updating diffusion.
scientific_constraints: Train every matched arm fresh with the same seed, damped-residual architecture, bounded state-diagonal diffusion, data split, normalization, lag, high-pass spatial mean, and saved 5 percent trimming rule.
Use the established horizons 2,5,10,20,30, mode counts 20,15,10,3,3, and particle counts 64,64,64,24,12 for every multistep arm.
Do not use endpoint mean or variance losses: this study isolates MC-GMM gradient routing.
The one-step NLL updates all jointly trainable drift and diffusion parameters in every arm. Only the MC-GMM gradient is routed selectively.
The MC-GMM term must never update diffusion in the stiffness-only, structured, or all-drift arms.
Compare energy, modal amplitude and covariance, PSD, ACF, rollout survival, and one-step NLL separately; do not select on NLL alone.
Tune and select only on validation repetitions 13 and 14; keep test repetitions 15 and 16 locked.
advisor_guidance: Run the four queued matched arms before making a decision: one-step-only, MC stiffness-only, MC structured stiffness-plus-damping, and MC all-drift. First test whether stiffness-only reproduces the amplitude and energy correction. If structured improves temporal behavior without amplitude loss, prefer it. Treat all-drift as evidence for whether the noisy residual MLP contributes useful signal. Do not add MC diffusion gradients. Promote at most one arm after the validation screens.

initial_trials.hypothesis: The matched one-step model retains substantial long-rollout amplitude excess without a closed-loop correction.
initial_trials.expected_observation: One-step NLL is competitive but energy and leading-mode covariance remain above the trimmed reference.

initial_trials.hypothesis: The relatively consistent MC-GMM stiffness gradient supplies most of the restoring correction needed to control amplitude.
initial_trials.expected_observation: Energy and leading-mode amplitude improve substantially without MC updates to damping, residual drift, or diffusion.

initial_trials.hypothesis: Routing MC-GMM gradients to stiffness and damping improves amplitude and temporal decorrelation while avoiding residual-network and diffusion noise.
initial_trials.expected_observation: Amplitude correction matches stiffness-only and ACF or PSD improves if damping carries useful multistep information.

initial_trials.hypothesis: The residual MLP provides additional useful closed-loop correction despite its noisier MC gradient.
initial_trials.expected_observation: All-drift outperforms structured-only only if the residual gradient contributes reproducible functional corrections.
